tsa-a10-v01.speaker: Teacher (kalādhvā-prakaraṇa)
tsa-a10-v01.question: What has just been stated?
premises: Thus, for now, the tattva-path is stated.
tsa-a10-v01.inference: The tattvādhva exposition stands concluded; the discourse is poised to turn.

tsa-a10-v02.speaker: Teacher (kalādhvā-prakaraṇa)
tsa-a10-v02.question: What is the kalā-path, and how does it differ?
premises: As in worlds something goes along as form — that is a tattva; so in the tattvas, class by class, whatever goes along as form — that is kalā.
Kalā is what endures one-form classifications (ekarūpakalanāsahiṣṇutvāt).
tsa-a10-v02.inference: Kalā is defined against tattva: same 'goes-along-as-form' pattern, but class-wise and classification-enduring — path distinguished from ground.

tsa-a10-v03.speaker: Teacher (kalādhvā-prakaraṇa)
tsa-a10-v03.question: How does nivṛtti behave?
premises: As in earth, nivṛtti turns back — from which the tattva-creation comes, it is said.
tsa-a10-v03.inference: Nivṛtti's turning-back is the source of tattva-sarga (cited via iti).

tsa-a10-v04.speaker: Teacher (kalādhvā-prakaraṇa)
tsa-a10-v04.question: What rules the water-class?
premises: In the class beginning with water, pratiṣṭhā as cause — by nourishment and filling.
tsa-a10-v04.inference: Pratiṣṭhā stands as kāraṇa in the jalādi-varge through āpyāyana-pūraṇa-kāritva.

tsa-a10-v05.speaker: Teacher (kalādhvā-prakaraṇa)
tsa-a10-v05.question: What rules the māyā-end class?
premises: In the class ending with māyā-of-puruṣa, vidyā — by the excess of consciousness over the disappearance of the knowable.
tsa-a10-v05.inference: Vidyā presides at the pumādimāyānte because saṃvid exceeds veda- disappearance.

tsa-a10-v06.speaker: Teacher (kalādhvā-prakaraṇa)
tsa-a10-v06.question: What rules the Śakti-end class?
premises: In the class ending with Śuddha-Vidyā-Śakti, śāntā — by the subsidence of the kañcuka-waves.
tsa-a10-v06.inference: Śāntā presides at the śaktyante through kañcuka-taraṅga-upaśama.

tsa-a10-v07.speaker: Teacher (kalādhvā-prakaraṇa)
tsa-a10-v07.question: Which four eggs are named?
premises: This very four-egg-group is the pārthiva-prākṛta-māyīya-śakti-named group.
tsa-a10-v07.inference: The catuṣṭaya (pārthiva, prākṛta, māyīya, śakti) is named as the four-egg group.

tsa-a10-v08.speaker: Teacher (kalādhvā-prakaraṇa)
tsa-a10-v08.question: What warrants aṇḍatva for these powers?
premises: In these, of the earth-and-rest powers, by their standing in the power-tattva as far as mutual contact exists, and contact's being with-obstacle — so much is warranted as egg-hood.
tsa-a10-v08.inference: Aṇḍatva is licensed exactly up to mutual-contact-with-obstacle in the śaktitattva — no further.

tsa-a10-v09.speaker: Teacher (kalādhvā-prakaraṇa)
tsa-a10-v09.question: What presides in the Śiva-tattva?
premises: In the Śiva-tattva, śāntātiśayā — because of the auspiciousness of its teaching-contemplation-arcā-beginning.
tsa-a10-v09.inference: Śāntātiśayā holds the śivatattve, grounded in the upadeśa-bhāvanā-arcā's kalyamānatva.

tsa-a10-v10.speaker: Teacher (kalādhvā-prakaraṇa)
tsa-a10-v10.question: What is beyond kalā?
premises: The autonomous, indeed, is the supreme tattva — that too, what is immeasurable, is beyond-kalā.
tsa-a10-v10.inference: The para-tattva's aprameya part is kalātīta — the measure exceeds itself.

tsa-a10-v11.speaker: Teacher (kalādhvā-prakaraṇa)
tsa-a10-v11.question: How do five kalās make thirty-six?
premises: Thus exactly five kalās make the thirty-six tattvas.
tsa-a10-v11.inference: Pañca-kalā × sapta-tattva = ṣaṭtriṃśat: the arithmetic of the scheme.

tsa-a10-v12.speaker: Teacher (kalādhvā-prakaraṇa)
tsa-a10-v12.question: How does prameyatva divide?
premises: Thus: prameyatva is twofold — gross-subtle; that makes ten.

tsa-a10-v13.speaker: Teacher (kalādhvā-prakaraṇa)
tsa-a10-v13.question: How does karaṇatva divide?
premises: Karaṇatva is twofold — pure and agent-touching; that makes ten.

tsa-a10-v14.speaker: Teacher (kalādhvā-prakaraṇa)
tsa-a10-v14.question: How is the thirty-sixth counted?
premises: By the distinctness of instrument-subordinate-agent-status: five pure-agent-status; five by undivided-division in expansion-facing; the Śiva-tattva, free of exhaustive-limitation, makes the thirty-sixth.
tsa-a10-v14.inference: From karaṇopasarjana-kartṛbhāva-sphuṭatva: five śuddha-kartṛ + five vikāsonmukha + Śiva-tattva = the thirty-sixth.

tsa-a10-v15.speaker: Teacher (kalādhvā-prakaraṇa)
tsa-a10-v15.question: Why is there no infinite regress?
premises: When taught or contemplated, its station is the thirty-seventh; contemplated again, the thirty-eighth — yet no anavasthā: knowing-making ends in the thirty-seventh itself, the thirty-sixth being transcendent-comprehensible; such the five-kalā rule.
tsa-a10-v15.inference: Contemplation would regress to 37, 38… but anavacchinnasvātantrya-yoga knowing ends at saptatriṃśa — the pañcakalā-vidhi closes the series.

tsa-a10-v16.speaker: Teacher (kalādhvā-prakaraṇa)
tsa-a10-v16.question: What is the three-tattva rule?
premises: The Ātma-kalā up to Vijñāna-kalā, Īśa-ending the Vidyā-kalā, the rest the Śiva-kalā: such the three-tattva rule.
tsa-a10-v16.inference: The five kalās regroup into three tattva-classes: ātmakalā, vidyākalā (īśānta), śivakalā.

tsa-a10-v17.speaker: Teacher (kalādhvā-prakaraṇa)
tsa-a10-v17.question: What follows by inference?
premises: Thus the ninety-tattva-and-rest too should be inferred — it is said.
tsa-a10-v17.inference: Navatattva-ādi extends the scheme by ūhāya — inference, not enumeration.

tsa-a10-v18.speaker: Teacher (kalādhvā-prakaraṇa)
tsa-a10-v18.question: What is the sixfoldness?
premises: Going-with-the-knowable-part triply by gross-subtle-other-nature: the bhuvanatattva-kalātmādhva-bheda named by mātṛviśrānti, likewise triply padā-dhvā (authority), mantra-dhvā (agitation-subsiding), varṇa-dhvā (full-knowership) — in such viśrānti one whose own-nature is gained: thus the one's sixfoldness is warranted.
tsa-a10-v18.inference: The ekasya ṣaḍvidhatva: one path, six facets — mātṛviśrānti names the triple distinction, and padā/mantra/varṇa-dhvā complete the six, closing in labdhasvarūpa.

sections.SUMMARY: Rite declared: the tattva-path stands stated. The kalā-path is delineated against it: whatever goes along as form class-wise — classification-enduring — is kalā. Nivṛtti turns back in earth, from which tattva-creation comes. Water-class: pratiṣṭhā as cause, by nourishment and filling. Māyā-end: vidyā, by consciousness exceeding the knowable's disappearance. Śakti-end: śāntā, by subsidence of the kañcuka-waves. The four-egg group bears the pārthiva-prākṛta-māyīya-śakti name. Egg-hood warranted only to mutual-contact-with-obstacle in the power-tattva. Śiva-tattva: śāntātiśayā, auspicious from its teaching-contemplation-arcā. The autonomous supreme tattva's immeasurable part is beyond kalā. Exactly five kalās make thirty-six tattvas. Prameyatva twofold — gross-subtle — makes ten. Karaṇatva twofold — pure, agent-touching — makes ten. Five pure-agent, five expansion-facing, Śiva-tattva free of exhaustive-limitation: the thirty-sixth. No infinite regress: knowing-making ends in the thirty-seventh itself, the thirty-sixth transcendent-comprehensible — such the five-kalā rule. Three-tattva rule: Ātma up to Vijñāna-kalā, Īśa-ended Vidyā, the rest Śiva. Ninety-tattva-and-rest inferred too — it is said. One path sixfold: mātṛviśrānti's triple distinction, padā-mantra-varṇa-dhvā — own-nature gained, warranted.
sections.FUNCTION: Delineates the kalā-path against the tattva-path, assigns class-presiding powers, counts the thirty-six, blocks the regress, and closes in the one path's sixfoldness.
sections.KEY TERMS: tattvādhva/kalādhvā (ground-path vs measure-path); nivṛtti (turning-back as sarga-source); pratiṣṭhā (water-class cause); aṇḍatva (egg-hood warranted to contact); pañcakalāvidhi (five-kalā rule); anavasthā (the blocked regress); ṣaḍvidhatva (the closing sixfoldness).
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Follows the tattvādhvā declaration (u1); the kalā arithmetic (u11-14), regress-block (u15), and dhvā-sixfoldness (u16-18) complete the scheme before the next prakaraṇa.
sections.BOUNDARY: The arithmetic is stated, not derived; ūhāya (u17) marks inference where enumeration stops; the regress-block rests on anavacchinnasvātantrya-yoga, asserted.
sections.EXPLANATION: Kalā differs from tattva only in being classification-enduring and class-wise; the powers presiding at each class-end (pratiṣṭhā, vidyā, śāntā) are causes of nourishment, consciousness-excess, and wave-subsidence respectively. Egg-hood runs exactly to mutual contact with obstacle. The count (10+10+5+5+1+...) reaches thirty-six, and contemplation's station would regress — but knowing-making, joined to undivided autonomy, ends at the thirty-seventh: no anavasthā. The five kalās regroup three-tattva, extend by ūhāya to ninety, and the single path discloses six facets closing in own-nature gained.
sections.RELATED: Tantrasāloka tattva-scheme parallels (lore support); no external translation witness — qa NEEDS_WITNESS expected.
